doc.title: Ray Drummond interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003

title: New professor job at Cal State Monterey Bay and coast-to-coast commuting
summary: Drummond describes his new tenure-track appointment at a young Cal State campus on former Fort Ord and his commuting from the East Coast, plus continuing gigs.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: California State University Monterey Bay, which is the former Fort Ord. So the federal government gave it to the State of California who in turn gave it to the California State University system. So up until this past semester we were the newest of the California State University campuses. There’s a new one now that has actually started this past September so we’re not the newest one, but we’re one of the smaller ones, we only have 3200 students and we’re eight years old.
How are you going to do that?

Well I’m not moving back to Monterey Bay anytime soon except maybe to get a place three or four years downstream. My family has lived in the Monterey Peninsula for the last forty years. So my pop passed away a couple of years ago and so my mom’s been living there by herself. And so it’s wonderful to see her prodigal son come back home, back there to hang out with her for various periods of time. Because it’s a full time appointment on the tenure track and all that.
Okay. So you’ll be doing some commuting from coast to coast?

Yes. I have been commuting. As the old vaudeville joke goes, and my arms are tired. Back and forth. I think it’s seven times since August, back and forth, seven or eight times. So it’ll probably continue maybe five times or so during the next semester. And then of course I’m free from the middle of May until the end of August. So I’ve been doing plenty of other gigs and still working with people like Kenny Barron and Toots © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

Thielmans, all during this time, from being there, and have some other projects that I’m involved in. One is a French project that takes me over there a couple of times a year minimum. And I would really like to get my own show back on the road but that’s had to take a back burner by necessity because there’s so much else going on.
